newsitem.title: UNITED NATIONS: Tanzania seeks more aid for Rwanda, Burundi refugees.
newsitem.headline: Tanzania seeks more aid for Rwanda, Burundi refugees.

text.p: President Benjamin Mkapa of Tanzania said on Friday his people's hospitality toward more than a million refugees from Rwanda and Burundi was wearing thin and he appealed to the international community to provide greater assistance.

In a speech to the General Assembly, he said one of the serious consequences of conflict in the region had been "massive human displacements and refugees which now constitute a tremendous burden to the neighbouring countries."
"Today, Tanzania is hosting over a million refugees from Rwanda and Burundi," he said, alluding to the effects of ethnic violence in both countries between majority Hutus and minority Tutsis.

The presence of such large numbers of refugees in limited localities had had a destructive impact on the environment, increased insecurity and criminality and imposed a heavy social and economic burden on host communities.
"The traditional hospitality of Tanzanians toward refugees is wearing very thin indeed," Mkapa said.

While the U.N. High Commissioner for Refugees and other humanitarian agencies had done useful work, it was not enough to offset the burden which these refugees placed on Tanzania's communities, he said.

"We call upon the international community, in the name of human solidarity, to redouble their assistance to meet the urgent needs of these refugees while at the same time addressing the long-term effects attendant on hosting them."

The ultimate goal must be their voluntary repatriation to their home copuntries, Mkapa said, adding: "To us, the creation of an environment that will facilitate such a process of repatriation is now a priority."
